name: boxd

modes.label: Pay as you go (credits, USD list)
modes.commit_note: No commitment. Custom plan offers volume pricing, but rates are not published.
modes.note: vCPU is billed on ACTIVE vCPU only, not the reserved shape size (checked 2026-11-08): "EUR 0.039 / USD 0.047 per vCPU-hour, on active vCPU only (not the vCPUs the machine reserves)" (https://boxd.sh/llms.txt); "You only pay for active vCPU, not for the vCPUs your machine reserves." (https://boxd.sh/pricing). cpu_util stands in for the active fraction (boxd says machines average about 10% active vCPU). RAM: "EUR 0.012 / USD 0.014 per GiB-hour, on memory actually resident"; ram_util stands in for resident fraction. Disk: "EUR 0.00008 / USD 0.000096 per GiB-hour, on disk written to". Sizes: "A machine comes in one of four sizes" (1/4, 2/8, 4/16, 8/32) and the default per-machine quota is 8 vCPU / 32 GiB (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources.md); the pricing page lists pay-as-you-go "Up to 8 vCPU · 32 GiB". The older FAQ line that 8/32 needs an email conflicts; the card follows the pricing page and resources guide. EUR list is the native list; the USD list is boxd's own separate list, not an FX conversion. Auto-hibernate after 4 h without inbound TCP/UDP traffic (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/suspend-resume). Whether page cache counts as resident is not documented.

evidence.quote: An empty list means no allowlist: the machine is unrestricted, which is how every machine starts.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve. Machine limit per org: 50 in the resources guide, 100 on the pricing page and llms.txt (card uses the lower 50); the limit applies separately in each region (Frankfurt, New York). 2 machines without a payment method. Sizes 1/4, 2/8, 4/16, 8/32; pricing page: pay-as-you-go "Up to 8 vCPU · 32 GiB" (checked 2026-11-08). Prepaid credits with $20 auto top-up.

plans.name: Pay as you go (machine limit raised on request)
plans.note: Ask boxd for a higher machine limit: "Ask for the new total you want, above your current limit and up to 1000"; above 1000, email contact@boxd.sh (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources.md, checked 2026-11-08). Sizes above 8 vCPU / 32 GiB are not published.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: Scale (pricing page): more than 100 machines, sizes above 8 vCPU / 32 GiB, "Our cloud or BYOC", dedicated support. SAML SSO on request for Enterprise (FAQ). Self-host: annual licence, free up to 16 vCPUs. No published prices. Audit logs are not listed on the pricing page (checked 2026-11-08).

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Share of session running (rest hibernated)
knobs.why: boxd bills active vCPU + resident RAM only while running; a hibernated machine (memory written to disk) pays written disk only. Use <1 if machines hibernate during idle gaps. Standby (auto-suspend) drops vCPU but keeps billing resident RAM per the pricing FAQ, so it saves less than hibernate.

knobs.label: Idle tail before auto-hibernate (x session hours)
knobs.why: Auto-hibernate triggers only after 4 h with no network traffic (default; it watches network, not CPU). A machine left alone after its work keeps billing active vCPU + resident RAM for up to 4 h. Since vCPU bills on active use, an idle tail costs mostly RAM. Factor = (session + idle tail) / session; the 5x max is the worst case for 1 h sessions.

caveats: Price history (v8-history audit): the 2026-05-26 archived pricing page advertised Individual EUR 20/month in its headline but 'EUR 0 forever, no credit card' in its own FAQ (team FAQ EUR 25-200/user/month); actual old invoice terms unknown. By 2026-08-31 it had moved to the current credit-metered regime (EUR 0.049/vCPU-h, EUR 0.015/used-GiB-h, EUR 0.0001/written-GiB-h, EUR 30 starting credit; live-checked 2026-09-28). A regime change, not a measurable discount; EUR->USD toggle differences are FX, not price changes. Then a ~20% rate cut, seen 2026-10-14: EUR 0.049 / 0.015 / 0.0001 -> EUR 0.039 / 0.012 / 0.00008 and USD 0.059 / 0.018 / 0.00012 -> USD 0.047 / 0.014 / 0.000096 per vCPU-h / GiB-h RAM / GiB-h disk (https://boxd.sh/llms.txt, https://boxd.sh/pricing).
EUR-native pricing. The USD list ($0.047 / $0.014 / $0.000096) is about 1.2x the EUR list (EUR 0.039 / 0.012 / 0.00008), checked 2026-10-14. EUR payers' USD cost depends on FX. Prices exclude VAT.
RAM is billed on resident memory, not the provisioned 4 GiB per vCPU. The estimate uses ram_util as the resident fraction. Whether page cache counts as resident is undocumented.

paused_ram_billed=true models STANDBY (optional auto-suspend: RAM + disk, no vCPU), per the pricing FAQ. The docs contradict this, calling standby 'near zero'. Default idle behaviour is HIBERNATE after 4 h without network traffic, which bills written disk only.

Idle timers watch network traffic, not CPU. A machine left running keeps billing active vCPU and resident RAM for up to 4 h (the default auto-hibernate window) after traffic stops. Disabling auto-hibernate means it keeps billing while it runs.

snapshot_gib_month uses the published written-disk rate ($0.000096 / GiB-h x 730 h), which applies to hibernated or stopped machines. Standalone named snapshots, backups (object storage, 7-day default retention) and volumes have no published price.
Disk is billed on bytes written, not the 100 GiB CoW provisioned. Forks share blocks.

Egress price not published (null): the rate card bills only vCPU, resident RAM and written disk, and the egress guide covers egress control only, with no transfer price or allowance (boxd.sh/pricing + docs.boxd.sh/guides/egress rendered 2026-09-28). Not assumed free. No dedicated IPv4: machines sit behind a shared proxy IP, with 3 raw TCP/UDP forwards per machine (docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources: 'a dedicated SSH port on boxd's shared proxy IP'). Note boxd.sh/faq marketing copy says each machine has 'a public IPv4'; the docs table is followed here (verified 2026-09-28).

Sizes 1/4, 2/8, 4/16 and 8/32 (vCPU / GiB). The pricing page lists pay-as-you-go "Up to 8 vCPU · 32 GiB" and the resources guide gives a default per-machine quota of 8 vCPU / 32 GiB; the FAQ still says 8/32 needs an email. The card follows the pricing page (checked 2026-11-08). No published ceiling above 8/32.

Resize exists but is not live: "boxd machine resize myapp --memory 16G" and "A running machine reboots to apply it, so its disk persists and running processes are lost." (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources, 2026-10-14). live_resize stays false.

Custom root images are possible only with boxd's help: "Machines boot from a container image, so a base like SUSE with your packages works. We set it up with you for now." The kernel stays boxd's (https://boxd.sh/faq/, 2026-10-14). image_oci stays false because you can't do it yourself yet.

Two regions: "boxd runs in two regions, and every org can use both." Frankfurt (fra) and New York (nyc). The machine limit "is set once and counts each region on its own" (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/regions, checked 2026-11-08). The FAQ still has an older US-waitlist line.
min_billed_seconds=0: the vendor says 'metered every second' and publishes no minimum.
No benchmark data for boxd in benchmarks.json. The vendor claims <10 ms boot and ~85 ms wake from hibernate.

Idle suspension on boxd is two-stage: auto-suspend (standby) stops vCPU billing but keeps billing resident RAM + written disk; only hibernate (default after 4 h without inbound traffic) drops to disk only. The engine's idle auto-suspend saving (auto_stop_idle) removes whole hours and so overstates savings for short idle gaps; use running_pct / hibernate_tail instead.

The vendor's own pricing-page calculator prices standby: 'Personal assistant' = 1 h/day running at $0.1564/h + 4 h/day standby at $0.0384/h (2 GiB resident x $0.018 + 20 GiB written x $0.00012) + 19 h/day hibernated at $0.0024/h = $10.82/month (730 h month). This confirms paused_ram_billed=true on the pricing page itself; the docs still say standby costs 'near zero' (checked 2026-09-29). Those figures use the pre-cut rates; at the 2026-10-14 rates the same example is about 20% lower.

Currency is fixed per organization at creation (EUR or USD list), and prepaid credit purchases/top-ups are non-refundable per the Terms (last updated 2026-05-08). An org cannot switch to whichever list is cheaper at current FX.

Billing basis change seen 2026-11-08: vCPU moved from full shape size while running to active vCPU only (https://boxd.sh/pricing, https://boxd.sh/llms.txt). Rates unchanged since 2026-10-14. The estimate uses cpu_util as the active fraction, so a mostly idle machine costs much less than its shape.

Machine limit: the resources guide says 50 per organization; the pricing page and llms.txt say 100. The card uses 50. Owners can ask for up to 1000 (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/resources.md, checked 2026-11-08).

Self-hosting uses an annual licence priced by cluster size, but "It is free up to 16 vCPUs, and a licence lifts that limit." (https://boxd.sh/pricing, checked 2026-11-08). SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are listed as "In progress".

Checkpoints: up to 10 per machine, memory and disk, restored in place (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/checkpoints.md). Disk backups to object storage on a schedule (https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/disaster-recovery). TS/Python SDKs and a gRPC API (https://docs.boxd.sh/llms.txt).

fleet.verification: Adding a payment card unlocks 50 machines and introductory credits; no charge just for adding card. Automatic wallet refills can charge thereafter.
fleet.tiers: New org without payment method 2; card on file 50 per organization per region (pricing page says 100); ask for up to 1000; above 1000 by email contact@boxd.sh.
fleet.notes: Resources guide: "Ask for the new total you want, above your current limit and up to 1000"; requests generally approved the same day (encoded as within 1 day, not an SLA). Hibernated machines count too. The limit "is set once and counts each region on its own" (Frankfurt and New York). A personal context counts as its own org, so one user with a personal context plus a team org has two separate quotas (and two credit balances).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

mcp_server.quote: Connect Linear, GitHub, Slack and over a hundred other integrations, then let scripts run on schedules and events while the machine sleeps between runs.
mcp_server.note: Not published: the docs index (docs.boxd.sh/llms.txt) and boxd.sh/llms.txt list no boxd MCP server for managing machines; the only MCP item is a blog post on hosting MCP servers. Was true with no source.

audit_logs.note: Not published: the pricing page (Scale and Self-host columns) and the docs index no longer mention audit logs. Was true with no source.

sso.quote: You sign in with GitHub or Google. Talk to us about SAML SSO for Enterprise.
sso.note: Sales-only (Enterprise). Self-serve sign-in is GitHub or Google.

desktop.quote: Desktop needs the default machine image at a recent version.
desktop.note: Built into the default image: open it from the console (Open > Desktop), `boxd machine desktop myapp`, or the SDK desktopUrl. Not on custom images or machines created before the desktop shipped.

snapshot_auto.quote: On by default, set to 4 hours. After 4 hours of no inbound TCP/UDP traffic, boxd hibernates the machine: a snapshot is written to disk and its memory is released.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: no inbound network traffic (not CPU idleness) for the auto-hibernate timeout (default 4 h, configurable, 0 = never). Memory, processes and open sockets included; wakes in ~85 ms on the next inbound packet. Optional auto-suspend (off by default) freezes the VM in host RAM after N s idle. Separate: scheduled disk backups to object storage (disaster-recovery guide), not counted here.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a saved copy of a specific machine. It captures the disk and the memory, so a machine booted from the snapshot is already running whatever the original machine was running (at time of snapshotting).
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. Named, versioned snapshots boot any number of new machines (`boxd machine new --from-snapshot`); machine must be running to snapshot; a machine can snapshot itself from inside. Also: checkpoints (memory+disk, up to 10 per machine, in-place restore), live fork of a running machine, manual pause/resume.

harness_api.quote: boxd machine exec myapp 'claude -p "Add a /health endpoint" --dangerously-skip-permissions'
harness_api.note: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode are preinstalled and pre-configured (agent_harnesses), with Claude Code login synced across machines, but the documented way to drive them from outside is the generic exec API/CLI or SSH + tmux + Claude's own /remote-control. No boxd API to start a prompt, stream agent events or list/resume sessions. The Claude Managed Agents / OpenAI Agents API integrations run Anthropic's/OpenAI's harness with boxd as the tool-execution environment (worker/executor inside the VM), not a boxd harness API.

egress_allowlist.quote: Two controls, both set from the SDK and enforced outside the machine, so nothing running inside it (root included) can loosen them: An egress allowlist per machine: the hosts and addresses it may reach. Everything else is blocked.
egress_allowlist.note: Entries: exact hostnames, wildcards (*.npmjs.org; refused on shared-hosting domains), public IPv4 addresses and CIDRs. HTTP(S) admitted by hostname, other protocols by destination IP. Changes live within a second. Set via SDK/gRPC (SetVmEgressAllow) only, not the laptop CLI yet. Default: unrestricted. `--isolated` additionally cuts the machine off from your own fleet. No IPv6 egress.

egress_http_rules.quote: Entries are bare hosts and addresses: no scheme, port, or path.
egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist is host/IP only; no method/path/header rules documented. (The secret proxy does rewrite HTTPS to bound hosts, but only for placeholder substitution.)

ingress_rules.quote: Serve your whole org over your company tailnet. Same hostnames, same TLS, reachable only from inside your Tailscale network.
ingress_rules.note: By default every machine has a public HTTPS proxy name.boxd.sh -> port 8000; you choose which extra ports get subdomain proxies and up to 3 raw TCP/UDP forwards (owner-only). Tailnet-only mode is org-wide and enabled by contacting boxd; bot protection (browser check) on wake. No per-machine IP allowlist or authenticated preview URL documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Code in the sandbox can run Docker, load kernel modules, restart `systemd`, edit `/etc`, open ports, and break the OS completely
guest_firewall.note: KVM microVM with its own kernel and network stack, root inside; nftables/iptables not explicitly documented but Docker (which programs iptables) runs natively.

secret_proxy.quote: Inside the machine `STRIPE_KEY` is an opaque string starting with `bxds_`. A request to `api.stripe.com` that carries it, in a header, the query string, the body, or Basic auth, arrives at Stripe with the real key. A request anywhere else carries the useless placeholder.
secret_proxy.note: Any secret can be bound to arbitrary hosts (`domains`), org-level, applies to forks/restores. HTTPS is intercepted with a boxd CA the VM trusts (cert-pinning tools fail). HTTP(S) only; no mention of databases/SSH/git-over-SSH. Separately, unbound secrets are injected as real env vars.

volume_attach.note: Persistent disks, created writable, attachable read-write or read-only, at create time (volumes=[VolumeMount]) or later; not combinable with --from-snapshot at creation. No published price.

volume_shared.quote: For now a disk can only be attached to one VM at a time (regardless of mode) — its backing file lives on one specific worker, not shared/networked storage, so this request is rejected if the disk already has any attachment.
volume_shared.note: Local worker-backed disk, one VM at a time even read-only. Forks get CoW copies, not a shared mount.

image_oci.quote: Machines boot from a container image, so a base like SUSE with your packages works. We set it up with you for now.
image_oci.note: Assisted only: boxd sets up a custom container base image with you; there is still no self-serve way (CLI/SDK) to boot your own Docker/OCI image, and the kernel stays boxd's. Self-serve starts are the default Ubuntu image, a fork, or a snapshot (`--from-snapshot`, https://docs.boxd.sh/use-cases/sandboxes). Kept false until it is self-serve.

anti_bot.quote: Stealth by default. The machine ships a Chromium build with anti-bot fingerprinting, and every launch gets a fresh fingerprint.
anti_bot.note: First-party `agent-browser` on every machine ships stealth/anti-fingerprinting Chromium, on by default, toggleable per launch.

captcha_solving.quote: The desktop is brought up automatically. ... click into it to help (type a password, solve a captcha).
captcha_solving.note: No automated CAPTCHA-solving service. CAPTCHAs are handled by a human opening the machine's Desktop and solving them manually mid-task, not by a built-in solver.

egress_ip_type.quote: Where are boxd machines hosted? In the EU by default, on European hardware, with no US cloud dependency.
egress_ip_type.note: Machines are KVM VMs on bare-metal servers in boxd datacenters (Frankfurt and New York); egress is from datacenter infrastructure, not residential/mobile IPs.

live_resize.quote: A running machine reboots to apply it, so its disk persists and running processes are lost.
live_resize.note: Resize now exists (`boxd machine resize myapp --memory 16G`) but a running machine reboots to apply it, so it is not a live resize: disk survives, processes do not. The old ChangeShape RPC (grpc-proto) was removed earlier.

own_agent_api.quote: boxd gives developers and AI agents their own persistent Linux machines accessible via SSH. No SDK required — if it can open an SSH connection, it can use boxd.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. boxd is infrastructure (VMs/sandboxes) for running your own or third-party coding/browser agents (Claude Code, Codex, agent-browser); it does not ship its own first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent with a driving API.

static_egress_ip.quote: Cloud accounts | The provider's SDK (`@aws-sdk/*`, `@google-cloud/*`, `@azure/*`) with credentials from `process.env`. The machine's outbound IP is fixed per cluster if you need to allow-list it
static_egress_ip.note: Outbound IP is fixed per cluster (shared among machines on that cluster), not a unique static IP per machine, but it is stable/allow-listable rather than rotating.

soc2.note: The pricing page lists SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 as in progress, not attested.

hipaa.quote: Our Services do not comply with industry-specific regulations such as HIPAA or FISMA. Users subject to such laws may not use the platform.
hipaa.note: Explicitly stated in the Terms of Service.

max_session_h.quote: A sandbox lives as long as you keep it, disk and all... boxd machines are natively persistent.
max_session_h.note: No maximum session/runtime duration is documented; machines run indefinitely until the owner stops/removes them (subject to idle auto-suspend/hibernate, which is configurable including disabled).

computer_use.quote: Desktop opens it in a separate browser window: a real desktop you can watch and control - launch a browser, a terminal, a file manager or any GUI app installed on the machine; type and click into whatever's running... Drive it from code: `browser.launch()` in an automation opens a Playwright-controlled browser on this same desktop.
computer_use.note: Desktop is a human-operated remote-viewer (mouse/keyboard for a person, or Playwright for browser automation), not a screenshot+click agent API. No documented API to drive the desktop by screenshots/coordinates.

public_ipv4.note: The only 'public IPv4' modeled in boxd's own protocol is a field on ProxyNodeInfo (cluster proxy infrastructure), not on the VM/machine resource. Docs elsewhere confirm: every machine's domain points at 'the proxy's shared public IP' and each machine gets 'a dedicated SSH port ... on boxd's shared proxy IP' plus up to 3 raw TCP/UDP forwards — i.e. one shared proxy IPv4 fronting many machines via SNI/port, not a dedicated public IPv4 per machine. boxd.sh/faq's marketing copy ('a public IPv4') is inconsistent with this technical description; the docs/proto description is treated as authoritative.

gpu.quote: Composable computers: persistent, forkable Linux VMs with their own kernel, a public IPv4, and an automatic HTTPS domain, reachable over SSH. Each machine is a real KVM virtual machine running Ubuntu 24.04 with 2 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, and 100 GiB persistent disk.
gpu.note: No GPU shape, GPU pricing, or GPU flag anywhere in the docs, pricing page, or FAQ; the only 'GPU' mention in the docs is about a customer's own external GPUs staying busy during RL rollouts, not boxd-supplied GPUs.

windows.quote: Each machine is a real KVM virtual machine running Ubuntu 24.04 with 2 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, and 100 GiB persistent disk.
windows.note: Product is Linux-only KVM microVMs (Ubuntu 24.04 image); no Windows guest image or option is documented anywhere. Outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: Each machine is a real KVM virtual machine running Ubuntu 24.04 with 2 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, and 100 GiB persistent disk.
macos.note: Only the CLI/client binary runs on macOS (Apple Silicon) as a laptop tool; the actual boxd machines are Linux KVM VMs. No macOS guest machine offering. Outside the product's scope.

arm64.note: VM creation config exposes no architecture/platform field, and no page advertises an arm64 guest machine option. 'The installer puts the boxd binary in ~/.local/bin/boxd. It supports macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x86_64 and arm64)' (docs.boxd.sh/cli/authentication-adjacent quickstart) describes only the CLI client host, not the VM guest architecture.

open_source.quote: Can boxd run inside my own cloud account (BYOC)? Yes — self-host the binary in your VPC, datacenter, or region. The open-source microVM engine underneath (Ignition) lives at github.com/lttle-cloud/ignition.
open_source.note: Only the underlying microVM engine (Ignition, AGPL-3.0 on GitHub) is open source; boxd itself (the API/control-plane/CLI/console product being priced) is a closed, signed binary distributed under a paid self-host/BYOC annual licence, not released under an OSI license.

nested_virt.quote: built on KVM, and a lightweight orchestration layer
nested_virt.note: derived: boxd machines are KVM microVMs (the open-source Ignition engine underneath). Neither boxd's docs, FAQ, nor the Ignition project page mention /dev/kvm passthrough or nested virtualization anywhere; the sandboxes guide describes root, Docker, kernel modules and systemd inside the guest but never hardware-virtualization extensions. Consistent with how this class of microVM sandbox (Firecracker/cloud-hypervisor-style) is documented by comparable providers, which do not expose nested KVM to guests.

usage_api.quote: rpc GetOrgBilling(GetOrgBillingRequest) returns (GetOrgBillingResponse); The org's shared plan: aggregate quota + current usage. Per-VM billing line items (admin only). Usage accrued but not yet charged, micro-euros. repeated OrgBilledVm vms.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; GetOrgBilling endpoint returns per-VM billing line items with accruing_micro_eur (usage cost), balance_micro_eur (credit balance), and billing_mode. GetBilling RPC for individual user billing. Requires JWT (interactive login, not just API key). Cost returned in micro-euros.

regions.quote: boxd runs in two regions, and every org can use both.
regions.note: Frankfurt (fra) and New York (nyc), same account, login and billing. The machine limit counts each region on its own.

self_host.quote: It is free up to 16 vCPUs, and a licence lifts that limit.
self_host.note: Self-hosting on AWS, GCP or any KVM host; annual licence above 16 vCPUs, price not published.

locations_quote: boxd runs in two regions, and every org can use both.
locations_note: Frankfurt (fra) and New York (nyc). The machine limit applies separately in each region. The FAQ still has an older US-waitlist line.
